newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania T-bill issue oversubscribed, yields slip.
newsitem.headline: Romania T-bill issue oversubscribed, yields slip.

text.p: An issue of 500.48 billion lei in Romanian three-month treasury bills was oversubscribed on Tuesday with bids by 13 banks exceeding by 240.5 billion lei the finance ministry's offer, central bank (BNR) data showed.

The bills, placed through a Dutch-style auction, offer an annual yield of 100 percent, down from the previous 104 percent. Banks' bids on Tuesday ranged from 80 percent to 150 percent, BNR data showed.
Around 95 percent of the issue was bought by commercial banks operating in Romania, including branches and subsidiaries of foreign banks. The rest went to their corporate clients.
The issue date for the fixed-interest bills with a face value of 10 million lei is May 8.
Over the the past months the finance ministry had several issues of bills with high annual yields, which reached almost 300 percent for floating rate papers.

Traders said returns have recently started to fall in line with a gradual ease in the BNR's monetary policy, which depressed short-term money market rates to some 100 percent this week, from about 220 percent in March.
They also said a recent finance ministry move to shift the yield calculation for 91-day floating-rate T-bills issued in February and March would trigger a further slide in returns.
The annual yield for floating-bills had been calculated previously at the BNR's average auctioned credit rates for their life period.

After the BNR scrapped the refinancing auction system last month the ministry pegged the bills' yields to the Bucharest Interbank Offered Rate (BUBID) for one-week funds set every Friday. Traders said one-week BUBID was 95 percent last Friday. ($=7,092 lei)
